classification.difficultyReason: Form the angle to due south, find an airport separation and invert the resulting direction for a bearing.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows an aeroplane that was flying towards an airport at $A$ on a bearing of $135^\circ$T.
When it was at point $O$, 20 km away from the airport at $A$, the flight course was changed.
The aeroplane landed at an airport at $B$ directly south of $O$. The distance from $O$ to $B$ is 50 km.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16, aeroplane and triangle left of parts a–b
spec.description: Schematic triangle OAB with O above B, A right and slightly below O, and black dots at all three vertices. A north arrow extends above O and an unlabelled horizontal reference extends both ways through O. A grey vector aeroplane silhouette lies above-left, pointing down-right. No bearing label, angle arc or right-angle marker is added.
spec.mathematics: OA = 20 km; OB = 50 km; B directly south of O. The stem supplies bearing OA = 135°T. Preserve the source schematic slopes rather than infer an angle from them. O is a named geographical point and remains labelled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the distance between airport $A$ and airport $B$ is 38.5 km, correct to 1 d.p.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $\angle OBA$ to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\angle OBA}{20}&=\frac{\sin45^\circ}{\sqrt{2900-1000\sqrt2}}\\\sin\angle OBA&=\frac{20\sin45^\circ}{\sqrt{2900-1000\sqrt2}}\\\angle OBA&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{20\sin45^\circ}{\sqrt{2900-1000\sqrt2}}\right)\\\angle OBA&\approx22^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The supplementary angle and $45^\circ$ would exceed $180^\circ$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the bearing of the airport at $B$ from the airport at $A$?

answer.worked:
$BO$ points north, so the bearing of $A$ from $B$ is approximately $022^\circ\text{T}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of B from A}&=180^\circ+\angle OBA\\&\approx202^\circ\text{T}.\end{align*}$$
